items.context: Standards expect `cli/prompt-manager` but the built binary is `cli/pm`. The binary is a Go ELF executable built from `cli/main.go`. Other scenarios (e.g., swarm-manager, landing-page-business-suite) have their CLI binary under `cli/` as a Go build artifact. The standards checker looks for `cli/<scenario-name>` specifically.

options.label: Rename build output to prompt-manager
options.rationale: Change the Go build `-o` flag to output `cli/prompt-manager` instead of `cli/pm`. Clean, direct fix. May need to update `install.sh` and any scripts referencing `pm`. Recommended because it directly matches the standard without adding indirection.

options.label: Add symlink cli/prompt-manager → cli/pm
options.rationale: Keep `pm` as the built binary, add a symlink. Quick fix but adds indirection; symlinks can break in some packaging scenarios.

items.context: 12 requirements (REQ-P0-003, REQ-P0-005, REQ-P0-012, REQ-P0-016, REQ-P0-017, REQ-P1-023, REQ-P1-024, REQ-P1-030, REQ-P1-031, REQ-P2-004, REQ-P2-027, REQ-P2-028, REQ-P2-029) reference PRD sections that don't exist. Additionally, 4 P0 targets and 1 P1 target have no linked requirements at all. The PRD.md is 44KB and was last updated Feb 2.

options.label: Update prd_ref fields to point to existing PRD sections
options.rationale: Map each broken `prd_ref` to the correct existing section in PRD.md. Most likely the PRD was restructured and refs became stale. Also add requirement entries for the 5 unlinked targets. Recommended because it's the most accurate fix.

options.label: Add missing PRD sections for the referenced content
options.rationale: If the PRD genuinely lacks those sections, add them. More work and higher risk of introducing inconsistencies.

items.context: There are 154 low/medium/info violations alongside the 8 critical+high ones. The plan currently scopes only critical+high, but some low/medium fixes may be trivial (e.g., the resolveApiBase consolidation is HIGH, but adjacent cleanup could fix medium items too).

options.label: Fix only critical + high violations
options.rationale: Strictly minimize scope. 8 blocking violations is a clear target. Recommended because it matches the chore's purpose (fix tidiness failures) without scope creep.

options.label: Fix critical + high, plus any medium that are trivially adjacent
options.rationale: While fixing HIGH issues, also fix medium ones that are in the same file/area and take <5 min each. Slightly more work but better ROI per edit.

items.text: The GCT review identified 5 distinct test failure categories: (1) standards violations exceeding threshold, (2) docs validation, (3) UI unit tests, (4) CLI unknown-command exit code, (5) missing bas/registry.json. The standards failure (#1) will auto-resolve once critical+high violations are fixed. The remaining 4 are independent and can be parallelized.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections. Problem statement, scope, technical context, phased implementation strategy, testing plan, and definition of done are fully populated. Contract decisions and some risk details are pending workshop decisions.
